passages.text: O LORD, God of vengeance, O God of vengeance, shine forth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD brings vengeance.
God of vengeance, appear.
God, show Yourself.
passages.original: אֵל־ נְקָמ֥וֹת יְהוָ֑ה אֵ֖ל נְקָמ֣וֹת הוֹפִֽיַע׃

passages.text: Rise up, O Judge of the earth; render a reward to the proud.
passages.sermon:
God is the Judge of the earth.
God has authority over all people.
God, rise up and take action.
God, give the proud what they deserve.
passages.original: הִ֭נָּשֵׂא שֹׁפֵ֣ט הָאָ֑רֶץ הָשֵׁ֥ב גְּ֝מ֗וּל עַל־ גֵּאִֽים׃

passages.text: How long will the wicked, O LORD, how long will the wicked exult?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sees the wicked.
The wicked rejoice.
The speaker asks God a question.
The speaker says, “How long will the wicked rejoice?”
The speaker repeats, “O LORD, how long will the wicked exult?”
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַ֖י רְשָׁעִ֥ים׀ יְהוָ֑ה עַד־ מָ֝תַ֗י רְשָׁעִ֥ים יַעֲלֹֽזוּ׃

passages.text: They pour out arrogant words; all workers of iniquity boast.
passages.sermon: All workers of iniquity speak.\r\nThey pour out arrogant words.\r\nThey boast.
passages.original: יַבִּ֣יעוּ יְדַבְּר֣וּ עָתָ֑ק יִֽ֝תְאַמְּר֗וּ כָּל־ פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: They crush Your people, O LORD; they oppress Your heritage.
passages.sermon:
The wicked attack God’s people.
They crush the people who belong to the LORD.
They oppress those whom God calls His own.
They bring suffering to God’s chosen ones.
passages.original: עַמְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה יְדַכְּא֑וּ וְֽנַחֲלָתְךָ֥ יְעַנּֽוּ׃

passages.text: They kill the widow and the foreigner; they murder the fatherless.
passages.sermon:
Evil people kill widows.
Evil people kill foreigners.
Evil people murder orphans.
Widows have no husbands.
Foreigners live among people who are not their own.
Orphans have no parents.
Evil people attack those who are weak and alone.
passages.original: אַ֭לְמָנָה וְגֵ֣ר יַהֲרֹ֑גוּ וִֽיתוֹמִ֣ים יְרַצֵּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob pays no heed.”
passages.sermon:
Some people speak about the LORD.
They say, “The LORD does not see.”
They also speak about the God of Jacob.
They say, “The God of Jacob does not pay attention.”
passages.original: וַ֭יֹּ֣אמְרוּ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶה־ יָּ֑הּ וְלֹא־ יָ֝בִ֗ין אֱלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Take notice, O senseless among the people! O fools, when will you be wise?
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to the people.
He addresses those who are senseless.
He calls them fools.
He commands them to take notice.
He asks them a question.
He says, "When will you become wise?"
passages.original: בִּ֭ינוּ בֹּעֲרִ֣ים בָּעָ֑ם וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים מָתַ֥י תַּשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃

passages.text: He who affixed the ear, can He not hear? He who formed the eye, can He not see?
passages.sermon:
God created the ear.
God made the ear to hear.
God can hear.
God formed the eye.
God made the eye to see.
God can see.
passages.original: הֲנֹ֣טַֽע אֹ֭זֶן הֲלֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִֽם־ יֹ֥צֵֽר עַ֝֗יִן הֲלֹ֣א יַבִּֽיט׃

passages.text: He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline? He who teaches man, does He lack knowledge?
passages.sermon:
God admonishes the nations.
God disciplines them.
God teaches people knowledge.
God does not lack understanding.
passages.original: הֲיֹסֵ֣ר גּ֭וֹיִם הֲלֹ֣א יוֹכִ֑יחַ הַֽמְלַמֵּ֖ד אָדָ֣ם דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile.
passages.sermon: The LORD knows the thoughts of man.\r\nThe thoughts of man are futile.
passages.original: יְֽהוָ֗ה יֹ֭דֵעַ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָדָ֑ם כִּי־ הֵ֥מָּה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: Blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD, and teach from Your law, to grant him relief from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the one who disciplines people.
The LORD teaches people through His law.
A man is blessed when the LORD disciplines him.
A man is blessed when the LORD teaches him from His law.
The LORD gives this man relief in times of trouble.
The LORD protects this man until the wicked are destroyed.
The LORD prepares punishment for the wicked.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֤י׀ הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר־ תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ׃ לְהַשְׁקִ֣יט ל֭וֹ מִ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עַ֤ד יִכָּרֶ֖ה לָרָשָׁ֣ע שָֽׁחַת׃

passages.text: For the LORD will not forsake His people; He will never abandon His heritage.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is faithful.
The LORD has a people.
The LORD will not forsake His people.
The LORD has a heritage.
The LORD will never abandon His heritage.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לֹא־ יִטֹּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ וְ֝נַחֲלָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א יַעֲזֹֽב׃

passages.text: Surely judgment will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God will restore judgment to righteousness.
Judgment will become righteous again.
All people who are upright in heart will follow righteous judgment.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עַד־ צֶ֭דֶק יָשׁ֣וּב מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְ֝אַחֲרָ֗יו כָּל־ יִשְׁרֵי־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand for me against the workers of iniquity?
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks.
He faces wicked people.
He faces those who do evil.
He asks a question.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked?
Who will stand with me against those who do wrong?
passages.original: מִֽי־ יָק֣וּם לִ֭י עִם־ מְרֵעִ֑ים מִֽי־ יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב לִ֝י עִם־ פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Unless the LORD had been my helper, I would soon have dwelt in the abode of silence.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is my helper.
If the LORD had not helped me, I would have died.
My soul would have gone to silence.
I would have had no hope.
passages.original: לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י כִּמְעַ֓ט׀ שָֽׁכְנָ֖ה דוּמָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: If I say, “My foot is slipping,” Your loving devotion, O LORD, supports me.
passages.sermon:
I speak to the LORD.
I say, “My foot is slipping.”
The LORD shows loving devotion.
The LORD supports me.
passages.original: אִם־ אָ֭מַרְתִּי מָ֣טָה רַגְלִ֑י חַסְדְּךָ֥ יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִסְעָדֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: When anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to the LORD.
The psalmist feels many anxious thoughts inside.
These anxious thoughts overwhelm the psalmist.
The LORD gives comfort to the psalmist.
The LORD’s comfort brings delight to the psalmist’s soul.
passages.original: בְּרֹ֣ב שַׂרְעַפַּ֣י בְּקִרְבִּ֑י תַּ֝נְחוּמֶ֗יךָ יְֽשַׁעַשְׁע֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Can a corrupt throne be Your ally— one devising mischief by decree?
passages.sermon:
God is holy.
God is just.
A corrupt throne cannot be God's ally.
A corrupt throne creates evil by law.
A corrupt throne makes plans for wrongdoing.
God does not join with evil rulers.
passages.original: הַֽ֭יְחָבְרְךָ כִּסֵּ֣א הַוּ֑וֹת יֹצֵ֖ר עָמָ֣ל עֲלֵי־ חֹֽק׃

passages.text: They band together against the righteous and condemn the innocent to death.
passages.sermon:
Evil people join together.
They attack the righteous person.
They accuse the innocent person.
They declare the innocent person guilty.
They condemn the innocent person to death.
passages.original: יָ֭גוֹדּוּ עַל־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וְדָ֖ם נָקִ֣י יַרְשִֽׁיעוּ׃

passages.text: But the LORD has been my stronghold, and my God is my rock of refuge.
passages.sermon: The LORD is my stronghold.\r\nMy God is my rock.\r\nMy God is my place of safety.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֬י יְהוָ֣ה לִ֣י לְמִשְׂגָּ֑ב וֵ֝אלֹהַ֗י לְצ֣וּר מַחְסִֽי׃

passages.text: He will bring upon them their own iniquity and destroy them for their wickedness. The LORD our God will destroy them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
The LORD will act against the wicked.
He will make their own sin return upon them.
He will destroy them because of their evil deeds.
The LORD our God will destroy them.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם׀ אֶת־ אוֹנָ֗ם וּבְרָעָתָ֥ם יַצְמִיתֵ֑ם יַ֝צְמִיתֵ֗ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
